scope.subject: Anatomy
scope.chapterTitle: Alimentary, Hepatobiliary systems, Pancreas and Spleen

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q011.takeaway: Gastroschisis results from an abdominal-wall closure defect and classically produces uncovered bowel through a usually right paraumbilical defect.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q011.displayText: The image is consistent with gastroschisis, caused by defective closure of the ventral body wall in the abdominal region. Intestinal loops herniate directly into the amniotic cavity, usually through a right-sided paraumbilical defect, and are not covered by an amniotic sac. This distinguishes gastroschisis from omphalocele, in which physiologically herniated bowel fails to return and remains membrane-covered at the umbilicus.
emphasis: defective closure of the ventral body wall
not covered by an amniotic sac

rationales.a: Failure of physiologically herniated intestinal loops to return produces omphalocele, a central membrane-covered umbilical defect, not gastroschisis.
rationales.c: Failure of body-wall closure in the pelvic region produces bladder or cloacal exstrophy rather than a paraumbilical gastroschisis defect.
rationales.d: Persistence or defective obliteration of the vitellointestinal duct produces anomalies such as Meckel diverticulum or an umbilical fistula, not gastroschisis.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q012.takeaway: Cloacal exstrophy reflects severe failure of ventral body-wall closure in the pelvic region, exposing bowel and paired hemibladders.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q012.displayText: The image represents cloacal exstrophy, caused by defective closure of the ventral body wall in the pelvic region. The characteristic appearance includes a central exstrophic bowel field flanked by two hemibladders; an omphalocele and defects of the anorectal and external genital structures may coexist. Cloacal exstrophy is more extensive than isolated bladder exstrophy because both urinary and intestinal structures derived from the cloacal region are involved.

rationales.a: Failure of intestinal loops to return from physiologic herniation causes omphalocele, not cloacal exstrophy.
rationales.b: An abdominal-region wall defect classically produces gastroschisis; this image-dependent condition is a pelvic-region closure defect.
rationales.d: Vitellointestinal-duct persistence causes ileal or umbilical remnants and does not account for the exposed bladder-and-bowel complex of cloacal exstrophy.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q013.takeaway: Gastrosplenic ligament is a dorsal-mesentery derivative; falciform/coronary ligaments and lesser omentum arise from ventral mesentery.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q013.displayText: The gastrosplenic ligament is not derived from the ventral mesentery; it develops from the dorsal mesogastrium. The ventral mesentery of the foregut gives rise to the lesser omentum and hepatic peritoneal ligaments, including the falciform and coronary ligaments. In contrast, derivatives associated with the spleen, including the gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments, arise from the dorsal mesogastrium.

rationales.a: The falciform ligament is a ventral-mesentery derivative associated with the developing liver, so it is not the exception.
rationales.b: The coronary ligament is derived from the ventral mesentery around the developing liver, so it is not the exception.
rationales.c: The lesser omentum is a classic derivative of the ventral mesogastrium and therefore belongs to the ventral mesentery.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q014.takeaway: Septum transversum is mesodermal and contributes to the diaphragm’s central tendon, liver connective tissue, and ventral foregut mesentery.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q014.displayText: The septum transversum develops from mesoderm. It is an early thick plate of mesoderm positioned between the developing thoracic region and yolk stalk and contributes importantly to separation of thoracic and abdominal compartments. Its derivatives include the central tendon of the diaphragm, connective-tissue stroma of the liver, and the ventral mesentery of the foregut.

rationales.a: Surface ectoderm forms epidermal and related structures and is not the germ-layer origin of the septum transversum.
rationales.c: Neuroectoderm forms the central nervous system and neural derivatives, not the septum transversum.
rationales.d: Endoderm forms epithelial components of the gut and organs such as hepatic parenchyma, but the septum transversum itself is mesodermal.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q015.takeaway: Ligamentum teres hepatis is a remnant of the left umbilical vein, not a septum-transversum derivative.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q015.displayText: Ligamentum teres is not derived from the septum transversum; it is the postnatal fibrous remnant of the left umbilical vein. The septum transversum contributes to the central tendon of the diaphragm, connective tissue of the liver, and ventral foregut mesentery. That ventral mesentery forms the lesser omentum and hepatic peritoneal ligaments such as the falciform and coronary ligaments.
emphasis: remnant of the left umbilical vein

rationales.a: The falciform ligament is formed from ventral mesentery associated with the septum transversum, so it is a septum-transversum derivative.
rationales.c: The coronary ligament is a hepatic peritoneal ligament derived from the ventral mesentery and therefore is linked to the septum transversum.
rationales.d: The lesser omentum develops from the ventral mesogastrium, a ventral-mesentery derivative of the septum transversum.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q016.takeaway: Liver, spleen and pancreatic buds develop in relation to the mesogastria; the kidney develops retroperitoneally from intermediate mesoderm.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q016.displayText: The kidney does not develop in the mesogastrium. The ventral mesogastrium is related to development of the liver, gallbladder and ventral pancreatic bud, whereas the dorsal mesogastrium contains the developing spleen and is related to the dorsal pancreatic bud. The kidney instead develops retroperitoneally from intermediate mesoderm through the nephrogenic system.
emphasis: kidney does not develop in the mesogastrium

rationales.a: The liver grows into the septum transversum within the ventral mesenteric region and is therefore related to the ventral mesogastrium.
rationales.b: The spleen develops from mesenchyme within the dorsal mesogastrium, so it is a mesogastrial structure.
rationales.d: The pancreatic buds develop from duodenal endoderm in relation to the dorsal and ventral mesenteries; the dorsal bud is specifically related to the dorsal mesogastrium.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q017.takeaway: Liver parenchyma is endodermal, but its fibrous/connective-tissue stroma comes from mesoderm of the septum transversum.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q017.displayText: The fibrous stroma of the liver is derived from mesoderm of the septum transversum. By contrast, the hepatic diverticulum is an endodermal outgrowth from the distal foregut; its proliferating epithelial cells form hepatocytes and the epithelial lining of the biliary passages. Thus the key distinction is endoderm for hepatic parenchyma and biliary epithelium versus septum-transversum mesoderm for the connective-tissue framework.

rationales.a: Foregut endoderm gives rise to the hepatic epithelial parenchyma and biliary epithelium, not the fibrous stromal framework asked here.
rationales.b: Midgut endoderm supplies midgut epithelial derivatives and is not the source of hepatic stroma.
rationales.c: Hindgut endoderm supplies distal intestinal epithelial derivatives and does not form the liver’s fibrous stroma.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q018.takeaway: The ventral pancreatic bud forms the uncinate process and inferior head; the dorsal bud forms the superior head, neck, body and tail.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q018.displayText: The false statement is that the uncinate process develops from the dorsal pancreatic bud. The uncinate process and inferior part of the pancreatic head arise from the ventral pancreatic bud. The dorsal pancreatic bud forms the superior part of the head, neck, body and tail, and its proximal duct may persist as the accessory pancreatic duct. Fusion follows rotation of the duodenum and brings the ventral bud posteriorly to the dorsal bud.
emphasis: superior part of the head, neck, body and tail

rationales.a: This is true: the inferior part of the pancreatic head is derived from the ventral pancreatic bud.
rationales.b: This is true: the accessory pancreatic duct is derived from the persisting proximal portion of the dorsal pancreatic duct.
rationales.c: This is true: the superior part of the pancreatic head is derived from the dorsal pancreatic bud.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q019.takeaway: Pancreas divisum is failure of fusion of the dorsal and ventral pancreatic duct systems, leaving separate drainage pathways.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q019.displayText: Pancreas divisum results from failure of fusion of the dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds and, critically, their duct systems. Normally most of the dorsal duct joins the ventral duct to form the main drainage pathway, while a proximal dorsal segment may persist as the accessory duct. When fusion fails, much of the pancreas continues to drain through the dorsal duct separately. This differs from annular pancreas, which reflects abnormal migration of the ventral pancreatic bud around the duodenum.

rationales.a: Persistence of a proximal dorsal duct segment normally contributes to the accessory pancreatic duct and by itself does not define pancreas divisum.
rationales.c: The dorsal pancreatic bud normally persists and forms much of the gland; failure of its regression is therefore not the mechanism of pancreas divisum.
rationales.d: The ventral pancreatic bud also normally persists, forming the uncinate process and inferior head; failure of its regression is not the mechanism.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q020.takeaway: The spleen is unusual among major foregut-associated organs because it develops from mesodermal mesenchyme in the dorsal mesogastrium.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q020.displayText: The spleen develops from mesodermal mesenchyme within the dorsal mesogastrium. Mesenchymal condensations form splenic lobules that later fuse, while mesoderm also forms the capsule, trabeculae and connective-tissue framework. As the spleen develops, the dorsal mesogastrium is remodeled into the gastrosplenic ligament anteriorly and the splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament posteriorly.

rationales.a: The ventral mesogastrium forms structures such as the lesser omentum and hepatic ligaments; it is not the site of splenic development.
rationales.c: The dorsal mesoduodenum is related to the duodenum and pancreas rather than the mesenchymal origin of the spleen.
rationales.d: Septum transversum contributes to liver connective tissue and the diaphragm’s central tendon, not to formation of the spleen.

marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q021.takeaway: The rectum has contributions from both hindgut and cloacal territory: proximal rectum from hindgut and distal rectum from dorsal cloaca.
marrow__ANAT_CH07_Q021.displayText: The rectum develops from both the hindgut and the cloacal region. The proximal part of the rectum is derived from hindgut, while the distal part develops from the dorsal portion of the cloaca as the cloaca is partitioned into anorectal and urogenital compartments. Therefore neither hindgut nor cloaca alone accounts for the complete rectal derivation tested by this question.
emphasis: both the hindgut and the cloacal region

rationales.a: Hindgut forms the proximal rectum, but this answer alone omits the distal rectal contribution from the dorsal cloacal region.
rationales.b: The cloacal region contributes distally, but it does not account for the proximal rectum derived from hindgut.
rationales.d: There are defined embryologic contributions from both hindgut and cloaca, so 'none of the above' is incorrect.
